partners.mechanism_chain: BLOC1S3 (HGNC:1400) —DISRUPTS→ BLOC-1 complex assembly and function (GO:0097212); DTNBP1 (HGNC:2790) —DISRUPTS→ BLOC-1 complex assembly and function (GO:0097212); BLOC-1 complex assembly and function (GO:0097212) —LEADS_TO→ Melanosome biogenesis (GO:0001734); BLOC-1 complex assembly and function (GO:0097212) —LEADS_TO→ Lysosome-related organelle biogenesis (GO:0034752); Melanosome biogenesis (GO:0001734) —LEADS_TO→ Albinism (HP:0001045); Melanosome biogenesis (GO:0001734) —LEADS_TO→ Platelet storage pool deficiency (HP:0001885); Lysosome-related organelle biogenesis (GO:0034752) —LEADS_TO→ Pulmonary fibrosis (HP:0002092); Lysosome-related organelle biogenesis (GO:0034752) —LEADS_TO→ Neutropenia (HP:0001874). Loss-of-function mutations in BLOC1S3 (causing HPS7) and DTNBP1 disrupt the assembly and function of the biogenesis of lysosome-related organelles complex 1 (BLOC-1). This complex is essential for the proper biogenesis of melanosomes and other lysosome-related organelles. Defects in melanosome biogenesis lead to albinism and platelet storage pool deficiency. Dysfunctional LRO biogenesis contributes to pulmonary fibrosis and neutropenia.

Loss-of-function mutations in BLOC1S3 impair lysosome-related organelle biogenesis, indirectly affecting cellular iron homeostasis. #### 1. Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome 7  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.486)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-432722)

**Proposed mechanism:** BLOC1S3 (HGNC:1400) —DISRUPTS→ BLOC-1 complex assembly and function (GO:0097212); DTNBP1 (HGNC:2790) —DISRUPTS→ BLOC-1 complex assembly and function (GO:0097212); BLOC-1 complex assembly and function (GO:0097212) —LEADS_TO→ Melanosome biogenesis (GO:0001734); BLOC-1 complex assembly and function (GO:0097212) —LEADS_TO→ Lysosome-related organelle biogenesis (GO:0034752); Melanosome biogenesis (GO:0001734) —LEADS_TO→ Albinism (HP:0001045); Melanosome biogenesis (GO:0001734) —LEADS_TO→ Platelet storage pool deficiency (HP:0001885); Lysosome-related organelle biogenesis (GO:0034752) —LEADS_TO→ Pulmonary fibrosis (HP:0002092); Lysosome-related organelle biogenesis (GO:0034752) —LEADS_TO→ Neutropenia (HP:0001874). Loss-of-function mutations in BLOC1S3 (causing HPS7) and DTNBP1 disrupt the assembly and function of the biogenesis of lysosome-related organelles complex 1 (BLOC-1). This complex is essential for the proper biogenesis of melanosomes and other lysosome-related organelles. Defects in melanosome biogenesis lead to albinism and platelet storage pool deficiency. Dysfunctional LRO biogenesis contributes to pulmonary fibrosis and neutropenia.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in BLOC1S3 or DTNBP1 in individuals with these phenotypes that do not cause loss-of-function, or the demonstration that these genes do not play a role in melanosome or LRO biogenesis, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: The presence of common, benign variants in BLOC1S3 or DTNBP1 in large population databases like gnomAD that are associated with these phenotypes.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism of BLOC-1 complex dysfunction in LRO biogenesis provides a potential avenue for therapeutic strategies targeting these pathways to ameliorate overlapping clinical features in both diseases.

#### 2. oculocerebrorenal syndrome  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.438)

Loss-of-function mutations in OCRL (Disease B) lead to impaired hydrolysis of PIP2, disrupting its metabolism and downstream cellular processes, resulting in renal tubule abnormalities. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in BLOC1S3 (Disease A) are hypothesized to indirectly disrupt PIP2 metabolism or its downstream effectors, leading to ocular abnormalities and intellectual disability, thereby converging on a shared disruption of PIP2 metabolic pathways.

**How to falsify it:** If genetic studies reveal that BLOC1S3 and OCRL act in entirely separate cellular pathways with no downstream functional overlap in phosphoinositide metabolism or related signaling, this hypothesis would be falsified. Additionally, the absence of shared phenotypic features beyond general categories in large patient cohorts would weaken the hypothesis. _(variant: Identification of common, benign variants in BLOC1S3 or OCRL in gnomAD populations that are not associated with either disease would suggest a lack of causal link or a very rare pathogenic mechanism.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role in phosphoinositide metabolism could reveal novel therapeutic targets for both diseases. Modulating PIP2 levels or related signaling pathways might offer a common therapeutic strategy for patients with either Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome type 10 or Dent disease, potentially improving renal function, cognitive deficits, and ocular health.
